findings.body: After this change merges, `forge next` can still name Codex for a ready part. `src/forge/nextstep.py:755-767` reads the configuration from the part’s starting branch, and `src/forge/task.py:590-600` uses the story branch when its plan has not landed on main. The approved `FORGE-RENDER-1` story is in that state: its branch still has `workers = "split"`, and its dependency-free `HELPER` part is not user-facing. Started parts have another gap: without a local settings file, `src/forge/nextstep.py:1162-1164` returns no builder name at all. The configuration change therefore does not satisfy the every-part outcome.
findings.title: Not done: forge.toml has workers = "claude" and forge next names Claude as the builder of every part

findings.body: The full test suite will fail with this setting. `tests/test_fix_the_owner_moved_this_repo_s_workers_from.py:46-48` reads this repository’s `forge.toml` and asserts that `workers` is `split`. `tests/test_source_split_workers.py:24-35` also uses this file and expects a plain task to start Codex. Those assertions must be updated for the owner’s new choice; otherwise the configured full test command and scheduled full-suite run remain red.
findings.title: Update the tests that still require split workers

findings.body: Changing this source repository from `split` to `claude` also changes how its user-facing story tasks are classified. With the default `tools = "both"`, `src/forge/repo.py:804-807` returns false for those tasks, so `src/forge/worker.py:187-199` uses the ordinary worker and build model instead of the frontend role and design model. For example, board work now receives the configured Claude build effort `low` rather than the design effort `high`, contrary to the existing user-facing routing contract. `tests/test_source_split_workers.py:17-21` exercises that distinction.
findings.title: Preserve design routing for user-facing source tasks
